intended_object: The canonical comparison functor from the category of descent data for a pseudofunctor F with respect to a family f i : X i ⟶ S, written with chosen pullbacks and triple fibre products (`DescentData'`), to the general category `F.DescentData f`. Each object and morphism keeps the same underlying data. This comes from the docstring and from its use as the `functor` field of `descentDataEquivalence`.
explanation:
The definition behaves as intended. On objects it sends D to `D.descentData`. That object has the same family `obj i`, and its gluing maps over any Y with q : Y ⟶ S are the pullbacks `pullHom'` of the chosen maps `D.hom i j`, taken along the induced map to the chosen pullback. This is the standard way to rebuild descent data in the general sense from descent data given on the chosen fibre products.

On morphisms it keeps the family `φ.hom`. The compatibility needed in `DescentData` is supplied by the lemma `comm`, which is proved from the compatibility on the chosen pullbacks. Functoriality holds by construction, since identities and compositions are computed componentwise in both categories.

This functor is one half of the equivalence `descentDataEquivalence`, whose inverse is `fromDescentDataFunctor`. No extra hypotheses are imposed: it works for any category C, any index type ι, any pseudofunctor to Cat, and any choice of pullbacks. So it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no separate declaration of this comparison functor besides this one and the equivalence built from it.
